questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend pinning only your three capstone projects instead of every repo you've ever created?
options: GitHub only allows six pinned repos, and a reviewer forms an opinion quickly, so three deep, complete projects beat many shallow ones
Older repos are automatically deleted by GitHub after one year
Pinning more than three repos is technically impossible on any GitHub account
Reviewers never look at pinned repos at all
questions.explain: The lesson explains that pinned slots are limited and a reviewer skims quickly, so a few complete, well-documented projects make a stronger impression than many unfinished ones.

questions.q: What is the first thing a strong AI-project README should lead with, according to the lesson?
options: A full license text with no other content
A one-sentence description of what the system does and who it's for
A complete list of every dependency version number
A blank page reserved for future notes
questions.explain: The lesson's five-part README structure opens with a one-sentence description before moving to architecture, demo link, eval results, and design decisions.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say an architecture diagram does more for a reviewer than paragraphs of description?
options: It shows in one glance that you understand how the system's pieces actually connect, which also prepares you for system-design interview questions
Diagrams are required by GitHub's terms of service for every repository
Paragraphs of text are not supported in Markdown README files
A diagram guarantees the code has no bugs
questions.explain: The lesson ties the diagram's value directly to demonstrating system understanding at a glance, which doubles as preparation for later system-design questions.

questions.q: What does the lesson say a short demo video or recording accomplishes that a README alone cannot?
options: It replaces the need for any code to exist in the repository
It lets a reviewer see the project's real, working behavior without cloning the repo and configuring it themselves
It automatically generates the project's eval numbers
It is required before GitHub will allow a repo to be pinned
questions.explain: The lesson notes most reviewers won't set up your environment themselves, so a short recording of real behavior gets most of the benefit of a live demo without that barrier.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what should you do before calling a portfolio project "portfolio-ready"?
options: Delete the README entirely so reviewers focus only on code
Remove all eval numbers in case they are later disproven
Add as many buzzwords as possible to the project description
Test every link in the README, since a dead demo link is worse than no link at all
questions.explain: The lesson lists a dead demo link as a common mistake and explicitly instructs testing every link before considering a project finished.
